editorial:
After a chance meeting, Kathy gets pulled into the world of the Vandals, a Midwestern motorcycle club led by charismatic Johnny. She falls for Benny, a quiet but intense rider who lives for the club. At first, the Vandals feel like a brotherhood built on freedom and loyalty. But as years pass, the club changes. New members bring violence, drugs, and crime, turning a tight-knit group into something darker. You watch Kathy struggle to hold onto Benny while the club pulls him deeper into danger. The story feels raw and real.

The acting is the real highlight. Jodie Comer shines as Kathy. Austin Butler brings cool, restless energy to Benny, while Tom Hardy is magnetic as Johnny. The pacing moves slowly at first, letting you soak in the mood, then picks up as the violence grows. The cinematography captures open roads and gritty clubhouses. The story can feel loose at times. Still, if you enjoy character-driven crime dramas with strong performances, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the Vandals have become a violent criminal gang, and Johnny is killed by a rival. Benny, torn between loyalty and love, finally walks away from the club with Kathy. They leave town and start a quieter life together. The movie ends with Kathy looking back on those years, realizing the brotherhood she once admired is gone. Benny's choice to leave shows that love and family matter more than blind loyalty to a gang.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven crime stories and strong performances.
